BatchCheckLayerAvailability.name: BatchCheckLayerAvailability
BatchCheckLayerAvailability.doc: Checks the availability of one or more image layers in a repository. When an image is pushed to a repository, each image layer is checked to verify if it has been uploaded before. If it has been uploaded, then the image layer is skipped. This operation is used by the Amazon ECR proxy and is not generally used by customers for pulling and pushing images. In most cases, you should use the docker…

BatchDeleteImage.name: BatchDeleteImage
BatchDeleteImage.doc: Deletes a list of specified images within a repository. Images are specified with either an imageTag or imageDigest. You can remove a tag from an image by specifying the image's tag in your request. When you remove the last tag from an image, the image is deleted from your repository. You can completely delete an image (and all of its tags) by specifying the image's digest in your request.

BatchGetImage.name: BatchGetImage
BatchGetImage.doc: Gets detailed information for an image. Images are specified with either an imageTag or imageDigest. When an image is pulled, the BatchGetImage API is called once to retrieve the image manifest.

BatchGetRepositoryScanningConfiguration.name: BatchGetRepositoryScanningConfiguration
BatchGetRepositoryScanningConfiguration.doc: Gets the scanning configuration for one or more repositories.

CompleteLayerUpload.name: CompleteLayerUpload
CompleteLayerUpload.doc: Informs Amazon ECR that the image layer upload has completed for a specified registry, repository name, and upload ID. You can optionally provide a sha256 digest of the image layer for data validation purposes. When an image is pushed, the CompleteLayerUpload API is called once per each new image layer to verify that the upload has completed. This operation is used by the Amazon ECR proxy and is…

CreatePullThroughCacheRule.name: CreatePullThroughCacheRule
CreatePullThroughCacheRule.doc: Creates a pull through cache rule. A pull through cache rule provides a way to cache images from an upstream registry source in your Amazon ECR private registry. For more information, see Using pull through cache rules in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

CreateRepository.name: CreateRepository
CreateRepository.doc: Creates a repository. For more information, see Amazon ECR repositories in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

CreateRepositoryCreationTemplate.name: CreateRepositoryCreationTemplate
CreateRepositoryCreationTemplate.doc: Creates a repository creation template. This template is used to define the settings for repositories created by Amazon ECR on your behalf. For example, repositories created through pull through cache actions. For more information, see Private repository creation templates in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

DeleteLifecyclePolicy.name: DeleteLifecyclePolicy
DeleteLifecyclePolicy.doc: Deletes the lifecycle policy associated with the specified repository.

DeletePullThroughCacheRule.name: DeletePullThroughCacheRule
DeletePullThroughCacheRule.doc: Deletes a pull through cache rule.

DeleteRepository.name: DeleteRepository
DeleteRepository.doc: Deletes a repository. If the repository isn't empty, you must either delete the contents of the repository or use the force option to delete the repository and have Amazon ECR delete all of its contents on your behalf.

DeleteRepositoryPolicy.name: DeleteRepositoryPolicy
DeleteRepositoryPolicy.doc: Deletes the repository policy associated with the specified repository.

DeleteSigningConfiguration.name: DeleteSigningConfiguration
DeleteSigningConfiguration.doc: Deletes the registry's signing configuration. Images pushed after deletion of the signing configuration will no longer be automatically signed. For more information, see Managed signing in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide. Deleting the signing configuration does not affect existing image signatures.

DeregisterPullTimeUpdateExclusion.name: DeregisterPullTimeUpdateExclusion
DeregisterPullTimeUpdateExclusion.doc: Removes a principal from the pull time update exclusion list for a registry. Once removed, Amazon ECR will resume updating the pull time if the specified principal pulls an image.

DescribeImageReplicationStatus.name: DescribeImageReplicationStatus
DescribeImageReplicationStatus.doc: Returns the replication status for a specified image.

DescribeImages.name: DescribeImages
DescribeImages.doc: Returns metadata about the images in a repository. Starting with Docker version 1.9, the Docker client compresses image layers before pushing them to a V2 Docker registry. The output of the docker images command shows the uncompressed image size. Therefore, Docker might return a larger image than the image shown in the Amazon Web Services Management Console. The new version of Amazon ECR Basic…

DescribeImageScanFindings.name: DescribeImageScanFindings
DescribeImageScanFindings.doc: Returns the scan findings for the specified image.

DescribeImageSigningStatus.name: DescribeImageSigningStatus
DescribeImageSigningStatus.doc: Returns the signing status for a specified image. If the image matched signing rules that reference different signing profiles, a status is returned for each profile. For more information, see Managed signing in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

DescribePullThroughCacheRules.name: DescribePullThroughCacheRules
DescribePullThroughCacheRules.doc: Returns the pull through cache rules for a registry.

DescribeRegistry.name: DescribeRegistry
DescribeRegistry.doc: Describes the settings for a registry. The replication configuration for a repository can be created or updated with the PutReplicationConfiguration API action.

DescribeRepositories.name: DescribeRepositories
DescribeRepositories.doc: Describes image repositories in a registry.

DescribeRepositoryCreationTemplates.name: DescribeRepositoryCreationTemplates
DescribeRepositoryCreationTemplates.doc: Returns details about the repository creation templates in a registry. The prefixes request parameter can be used to return the details for a specific repository creation template.

GetAccountSetting.name: GetAccountSetting
GetAccountSetting.doc: Retrieves the account setting value for the specified setting name.

GetAuthorizationToken.name: GetAuthorizationToken
GetAuthorizationToken.doc: Retrieves an authorization token. An authorization token represents your IAM authentication credentials and can be used to access any Amazon ECR registry that your IAM principal has access to. The authorization token is valid for 12 hours. The authorizationToken returned is a base64 encoded string that can be decoded and used in a docker login command to authenticate to a registry. The CLI offers…

GetDownloadUrlForLayer.name: GetDownloadUrlForLayer
GetDownloadUrlForLayer.doc: Retrieves the pre-signed Amazon S3 download URL corresponding to an image layer. You can only get URLs for image layers that are referenced in an image. When an image is pulled, the GetDownloadUrlForLayer API is called once per image layer that is not already cached. This operation is used by the Amazon ECR proxy and is not generally used by customers for pulling and pushing images. In most…

GetLifecyclePolicy.name: GetLifecyclePolicy
GetLifecyclePolicy.doc: Retrieves the lifecycle policy for the specified repository.

GetLifecyclePolicyPreview.name: GetLifecyclePolicyPreview
GetLifecyclePolicyPreview.doc: Retrieves the results of the lifecycle policy preview request for the specified repository.

GetRegistryPolicy.name: GetRegistryPolicy
GetRegistryPolicy.doc: Retrieves the permissions policy for a registry.

GetRegistryScanningConfiguration.name: GetRegistryScanningConfiguration
GetRegistryScanningConfiguration.doc: Retrieves the scanning configuration for a registry.

GetRepositoryPolicy.name: GetRepositoryPolicy
GetRepositoryPolicy.doc: Retrieves the repository policy for the specified repository.

GetSigningConfiguration.name: GetSigningConfiguration
GetSigningConfiguration.doc: Retrieves the registry's signing configuration, which defines rules for automatically signing images using Amazon Web Services Signer. For more information, see Managed signing in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

InitiateLayerUpload.name: InitiateLayerUpload
InitiateLayerUpload.doc: Notifies Amazon ECR that you intend to upload an image layer. When an image is pushed, the InitiateLayerUpload API is called once per image layer that has not already been uploaded. Whether or not an image layer has been uploaded is determined by the BatchCheckLayerAvailability API action. This operation is used by the Amazon ECR proxy and is not generally used by customers for pulling and…

ListImageReferrers.name: ListImageReferrers
ListImageReferrers.doc: Lists the artifacts associated with a specified subject image. The IAM principal invoking this operation must have the ecr:BatchGetImage permission.

ListImages.name: ListImages
ListImages.doc: Lists all the image IDs for the specified repository. You can filter images based on whether or not they are tagged by using the tagStatus filter and specifying either TAGGED, UNTAGGED or ANY. For example, you can filter your results to return only UNTAGGED images and then pipe that result to a BatchDeleteImage operation to delete them. Or, you can filter your results to return only TAGGED images…

ListPullTimeUpdateExclusions.name: ListPullTimeUpdateExclusions
ListPullTimeUpdateExclusions.doc: Lists the IAM principals that are excluded from having their image pull times recorded.

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.doc: List the tags for an Amazon ECR resource.

PutAccountSetting.name: PutAccountSetting
PutAccountSetting.doc: Allows you to change the basic scan type version or registry policy scope.

PutImage.name: PutImage
PutImage.doc: Creates or updates the image manifest and tags associated with an image. When an image is pushed and all new image layers have been uploaded, the PutImage API is called once to create or update the image manifest and the tags associated with the image. This operation is used by the Amazon ECR proxy and is not generally used by customers for pulling and pushing images. In most cases, you should…

PutImageScanningConfiguration.name: PutImageScanningConfiguration
PutImageScanningConfiguration.doc: The PutImageScanningConfiguration API is being deprecated, in favor of specifying the image scanning configuration at the registry level. For more information, see PutRegistryScanningConfiguration. Updates the image scanning configuration for the specified repository.

PutImageTagMutability.name: PutImageTagMutability
PutImageTagMutability.doc: Updates the image tag mutability settings for the specified repository. For more information, see Image tag mutability in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

PutLifecyclePolicy.name: PutLifecyclePolicy
PutLifecyclePolicy.doc: Creates or updates the lifecycle policy for the specified repository. For more information, see Lifecycle policy template.

PutRegistryPolicy.name: PutRegistryPolicy
PutRegistryPolicy.doc: Creates or updates the permissions policy for your registry. A registry policy is used to specify permissions for another Amazon Web Services account and is used when configuring cross-account replication. For more information, see Registry permissions in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

PutRegistryScanningConfiguration.name: PutRegistryScanningConfiguration
PutRegistryScanningConfiguration.doc: Creates or updates the scanning configuration for your private registry.

PutReplicationConfiguration.name: PutReplicationConfiguration
PutReplicationConfiguration.doc: Creates or updates the replication configuration for a registry. The existing replication configuration for a repository can be retrieved with the DescribeRegistry API action. The first time the PutReplicationConfiguration API is called, a service-linked IAM role is created in your account for the replication process. For more information, see Using service-linked roles for Amazon ECR in the…

PutSigningConfiguration.name: PutSigningConfiguration
PutSigningConfiguration.doc: Creates or updates the registry's signing configuration, which defines rules for automatically signing images with Amazon Web Services Signer. For more information, see Managed signing in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide. To successfully generate a signature, the IAM principal pushing images must have permission to sign payloads with the Amazon Web Services Signer signing profile…

RegisterPullTimeUpdateExclusion.name: RegisterPullTimeUpdateExclusion
RegisterPullTimeUpdateExclusion.doc: Adds an IAM principal to the pull time update exclusion list for a registry. Amazon ECR will not record the pull time if an excluded principal pulls an image.

SetRepositoryPolicy.name: SetRepositoryPolicy
SetRepositoryPolicy.doc: Applies a repository policy to the specified repository to control access permissions. For more information, see Amazon ECR Repository policies in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

StartImageScan.name: StartImageScan
StartImageScan.doc: Starts a basic image vulnerability scan. A basic image scan can only be started once per 24 hours on an individual image. This limit includes if an image was scanned on initial push. You can start up to 100,000 basic scans per 24 hours. This limit includes both scans on initial push and scans initiated by the StartImageScan API. For more information, see Basic scanning in the Amazon Elastic…

StartLifecyclePolicyPreview.name: StartLifecyclePolicyPreview
StartLifecyclePolicyPreview.doc: Starts a preview of a lifecycle policy for the specified repository. This allows you to see the results before associating the lifecycle policy with the repository.

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.doc: Adds specified tags to a resource with the specified ARN. Existing tags on a resource are not changed if they are not specified in the request parameters.

UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.doc: Deletes specified tags from a resource.

UpdateImageStorageClass.name: UpdateImageStorageClass
UpdateImageStorageClass.doc: Transitions an image between storage classes. You can transition images from Amazon ECR standard storage class to Amazon ECR archival storage class for long-term storage, or restore archived images back to Amazon ECR standard.

UpdatePullThroughCacheRule.name: UpdatePullThroughCacheRule
UpdatePullThroughCacheRule.doc: Updates an existing pull through cache rule.

UpdateRepositoryCreationTemplate.name: UpdateRepositoryCreationTemplate
UpdateRepositoryCreationTemplate.doc: Updates an existing repository creation template.

UploadLayerPart.name: UploadLayerPart
UploadLayerPart.doc: Uploads an image layer part to Amazon ECR. When an image is pushed, each new image layer is uploaded in parts. The maximum size of each image layer part can be 20971520 bytes (or about 20MB). The UploadLayerPart API is called once per each new image layer part. This operation is used by the Amazon ECR proxy and is not generally used by customers for pulling and pushing images. In most cases, you…

ValidatePullThroughCacheRule.name: ValidatePullThroughCacheRule
ValidatePullThroughCacheRule.doc: Validates an existing pull through cache rule for an upstream registry that requires authentication. This will retrieve the contents of the Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager secret, verify the syntax, and then validate that authentication to the upstream registry is successful.

The repository name must start with a letter and can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, and forward slashes.

description.doc: The description associated with the repository creation template.

encryptionConfiguration.doc: The encryption configuration associated with the repository creation template.

resourceTags.doc: The metadata to apply to the repository to help you categorize and organize. Each tag consists of a key and an optional value, both of which you define. Tag keys can have a maximum character length of 128 characters, and tag values can have a maximum length of 256 characters.

imageTagMutability.doc: The tag mutability setting for the repository. If this parameter is omitted, the default setting of MUTABLE will be used which will allow image tags to be overwritten. If IMMUTABLE is specified, all image tags within the repository will be immutable which will prevent them from being overwritten.

imageTagMutabilityExclusionFilters.doc: A list of filters that specify which image tags are excluded from the repository creation template's image tag mutability setting.

repositoryPolicy.doc: The repository policy to apply to repositories created using the template. A repository policy is a permissions policy associated with a repository to control access permissions.

lifecyclePolicy.doc: The lifecycle policy to use for repositories created using the template.

appliedFor.doc: A list of enumerable Strings representing the repository creation scenarios that this template will apply towards. The supported scenarios are PULL_THROUGH_CACHE, REPLICATION, and CREATE_ON_PUSH

customRoleArn.doc: The ARN of the role to be assumed by Amazon ECR. Amazon ECR will assume your supplied role when the customRoleArn is specified. When this field isn't specified, Amazon ECR will use the service-linked role for the repository creation template.

createdAt.doc: The date and time, in JavaScript date format, when the repository creation template was created.

updatedAt.doc: The date and time, in JavaScript date format, when the repository creation template was last updated.

RepositoryCreationTemplate.doc: The details of the repository creation template associated with the request.

filter.doc: The repository filter details. When the PREFIX_MATCH filter type is specified, this value is required and should be the repository name prefix to configure replication for.

filterType.doc: The repository filter type. The only supported value is PREFIX_MATCH, which is a repository name prefix specified with the filter parameter.

RepositoryFilter.doc: The filter settings used with image replication. Specifying a repository filter to a replication rule provides a method for controlling which repositories in a private registry are replicated. If no filters are added, the contents of all repositories are replicated.

repositoryName.doc: The name of the repository.

scanOnPush.doc: Whether or not scan on push is configured for the repository.

scanFrequency.doc: The scan frequency for the repository.

appliedScanFilters.doc: The scan filters applied to the repository.

RepositoryScanningConfiguration.doc: The details of the scanning configuration for a repository.

repositoryName.doc: The name of the repository.

RepositoryScanningConfigurationFailure.doc: The details about any failures associated with the scanning configuration of a repository.

details.doc: An object that contains details about the resource involved in a finding.

tags.doc: The tags attached to the resource.

Resource.doc: Details about the resource involved in a finding.

awsEcrContainerImage.doc: An object that contains details about the Amazon ECR container image involved in the finding.

ResourceDetails.doc: Contains details about the resource involved in the finding.

filter.doc: The filter to use when scanning.

filterType.doc: The type associated with the filter.

ScanningRepositoryFilter.doc: The details of a scanning repository filter. For more information on how to use filters, see Using filters in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

cvss.doc: An object that contains details about the CVSS score given to a finding.

ScoreDetails.doc: Information about the Amazon Inspector score given to a finding.

registryId.doc: The Amazon Web Services account ID associated with the registry that contains the repository. If you do not specify a registry, the default registry is assumed.

repositoryName.doc: The name of the repository to receive the policy.

policyText.doc: The JSON repository policy text to apply to the repository. For more information, see Amazon ECR repository policies in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

force.doc: If the policy you are attempting to set on a repository policy would prevent you from setting another policy in the future, you must force the SetRepositoryPolicy operation. This is intended to prevent accidental repository lock outs.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

repositoryName.doc: The repository name associated with the request.

policyText.doc: The JSON repository policy text applied to the repository.

rules.doc: A list of signing rules. Each rule defines a signing profile and optional repository filters that determine which images are automatically signed. Maximum of 10 rules.

SigningConfiguration.doc: The signing configuration for a registry, which specifies rules for automatically signing images when pushed.

SigningProfileArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Amazon Web Services Signer signing profile. The ARN contains the arn:aws:signer namespace, followed by the region, Amazon Web Services account ID, and signing profile resource path. For example, arn:aws:signer:region:012345678910:/signing-profiles/profile-name.

filter.doc: The filter value used to match repository names. When using WILDCARD_MATCH, the * character matches any sequence of characters. Examples: myapp/* - Matches all repositories starting with myapp/ */production - Matches all repositories ending with /production *prod* - Matches all repositories containing prod

filterType.doc: The type of filter to apply. Currently, only WILDCARD_MATCH is supported, which uses wildcard patterns to match repository names.

SigningRepositoryFilter.doc: A repository filter used to determine which repositories have their images automatically signed on push. Each filter consists of a filter type and filter value.

SigningRepositoryFilterType.doc: The type of filter to use when determining which repositories should have their images automatically signed.

signingProfileArn.doc: The ARN of the Amazon Web Services Signer signing profile to use for signing images that match this rule. For more information about signing profiles, see Signing profiles in the Amazon Web Services Signer Developer Guide.

repositoryFilters.doc: A list of repository filters that determine which repositories have their images signed on push. If no filters are specified, all images pushed to the registry are signed using the rule's signing profile. Maximum of 100 filters per rule.

SigningRule.doc: A signing rule that specifies a signing profile and optional repository filters. When an image is pushed to a matching repository, a signing job is created using the specified profile.

SigningStatus.doc: The image signing status. Possible values include IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, and FAILED.

registryId.doc: The Amazon Web Services account ID associated with the registry that contains the repository in which to start an image scan request. If you do not specify a registry, the default registry is assumed.

repositoryName.doc: The name of the repository that contains the images to scan.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

repositoryName.doc: The repository name associated with the request.

imageScanStatus.doc: The current state of the scan.

registryId.doc: The Amazon Web Services account ID associated with the registry that contains the repository. If you do not specify a registry, the default registry is assumed.

repositoryName.doc: The name of the repository to be evaluated.

lifecyclePolicyText.doc: The policy to be evaluated against. If you do not specify a policy, the current policy for the repository is used.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

repositoryName.doc: The repository name associated with the request.

status.doc: The status of the lifecycle policy preview request.

SubjectIdentifier.doc: An object that identifies an image subject.

Key.doc: One part of a key-value pair that make up a tag. A key is a general label that acts like a category for more specific tag values.

Value.doc: A value acts as a descriptor within a tag category (key).

Tag.doc: The metadata to apply to a resource to help you categorize and organize them. Each tag consists of a key and a value, both of which you define. Tag keys can have a maximum character length of 128 characters, and tag values can have a maximum length of 256 characters.

resourceArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the the resource to which to add tags. Currently, the only supported resource is an Amazon ECR repository.

tags.doc: The tags to add to the resource. A tag is an array of key-value pairs. Tag keys can have a maximum character length of 128 characters, and tag values can have a maximum length of 256 characters.

imageTotalCount.doc: The total number of images transitioning to the storage class.

TransitioningImageTotalCount.doc: The total count of images transitioning to a storage class.

resourceArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource from which to remove tags. Currently, the only supported resource is an Amazon ECR repository.

tagKeys.doc: The keys of the tags to be removed.

registryId.doc: The Amazon Web Services account ID associated with the registry that contains the image to transition. If you do not specify a registry, the default registry is assumed.

repositoryName.doc: The name of the repository that contains the image to transition.

targetStorageClass.doc: The target storage class for the image.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

repositoryName.doc: The repository name associated with the request.

imageStatus.doc: The current status of the image after the call to UpdateImageStorageClass is complete. Valid values are ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, and ACTIVATING.

registryId.doc: The Amazon Web Services account ID associated with the registry associated with the pull through cache rule. If you do not specify a registry, the default registry is assumed.

ecrRepositoryPrefix.doc: The repository name prefix to use when caching images from the source registry.

credentialArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager secret that identifies the credentials to authenticate to the upstream registry.

customRoleArn.doc: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role to be assumed by Amazon ECR to authenticate to the ECR upstream registry. This role must be in the same account as the registry that you are configuring.

ecrRepositoryPrefix.doc: The Amazon ECR repository prefix associated with the pull through cache rule.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

updatedAt.doc: The date and time, in JavaScript date format, when the pull through cache rule was updated.

credentialArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager secret associated with the pull through cache rule.

customRoleArn.doc: The ARN of the IAM role associated with the pull through cache rule.

upstreamRepositoryPrefix.doc: The upstream repository prefix associated with the pull through cache rule.

prefix.doc: The repository namespace prefix that matches an existing repository creation template in the registry. All repositories created using this namespace prefix will have the settings defined in this template applied. For example, a prefix of prod would apply to all repositories beginning with prod/. This includes a repository named prod/team1 as well as a repository named prod/repository1. To apply a…

description.doc: A description for the repository creation template.

resourceTags.doc: The metadata to apply to the repository to help you categorize and organize. Each tag consists of a key and an optional value, both of which you define. Tag keys can have a maximum character length of 128 characters, and tag values can have a maximum length of 256 characters.

imageTagMutability.doc: Updates the tag mutability setting for the repository. If this parameter is omitted, the default setting of MUTABLE will be used which will allow image tags to be overwritten. If IMMUTABLE is specified, all image tags within the repository will be immutable which will prevent them from being overwritten.

imageTagMutabilityExclusionFilters.doc: A list of filters that specify which image tags should be excluded from the repository creation template's image tag mutability setting.

repositoryPolicy.doc: Updates the repository policy created using the template. A repository policy is a permissions policy associated with a repository to control access permissions.

lifecyclePolicy.doc: Updates the lifecycle policy associated with the specified repository creation template.

appliedFor.doc: Updates the list of enumerable strings representing the Amazon ECR repository creation scenarios that this template will apply towards. The supported scenarios are PULL_THROUGH_CACHE, REPLICATION, and CREATE_ON_PUSH

customRoleArn.doc: The ARN of the role to be assumed by Amazon ECR. This role must be in the same account as the registry that you are configuring. Amazon ECR will assume your supplied role when the customRoleArn is specified. When this field isn't specified, Amazon ECR will use the service-linked role for the repository creation template.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

repositoryCreationTemplate.doc: The details of the repository creation template associated with the request.

registryId.doc: The Amazon Web Services account ID associated with the registry to which you are uploading layer parts. If you do not specify a registry, the default registry is assumed.

repositoryName.doc: The name of the repository to which you are uploading layer parts.

uploadId.doc: The upload ID from a previous InitiateLayerUpload operation to associate with the layer part upload.

partFirstByte.doc: The position of the first byte of the layer part witin the overall image layer.

partLastByte.doc: The position of the last byte of the layer part within the overall image layer.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

repositoryName.doc: The repository name associated with the request.

uploadId.doc: The upload ID associated with the request.

lastByteReceived.doc: The integer value of the last byte received in the request.

ecrRepositoryPrefix.doc: The repository name prefix associated with the pull through cache rule.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the pull through cache rule. If you do not specify a registry, the default registry is assumed.

ecrRepositoryPrefix.doc: The Amazon ECR repository prefix associated with the pull through cache rule.

registryId.doc: The registry ID associated with the request.

upstreamRegistryUrl.doc: The upstream registry URL associated with the pull through cache rule.

credentialArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager secret associated with the pull through cache rule.

customRoleArn.doc: The ARN of the IAM role associated with the pull through cache rule.

upstreamRepositoryPrefix.doc: The upstream repository prefix associated with the pull through cache rule.

isValid.doc: Whether or not the pull through cache rule was validated. If true, Amazon ECR was able to reach the upstream registry and authentication was successful. If false, there was an issue and validation failed. The failure reason indicates the cause.

failure.doc: The reason the validation failed. For more details about possible causes and how to address them, see Using pull through cache rules in the Amazon Elastic Container Registry User Guide.

arch.doc: The architecture of the vulnerable package.

epoch.doc: The epoch of the vulnerable package.

filePath.doc: The file path of the vulnerable package.

name.doc: The name of the vulnerable package.

packageManager.doc: The package manager of the vulnerable package.

release.doc: The release of the vulnerable package.

sourceLayerHash.doc: The source layer hash of the vulnerable package.

version.doc: The version of the vulnerable package.

fixedInVersion.doc: The version of the package that contains the vulnerability fix.

VulnerablePackage.doc: Information on the vulnerable package identified by a finding.
